angle: Movement translation for receivers (WR/TE, chosen because it is the only group with graded drill cuts and matched NFL route families on both sides): per-receiver Cut Match = gap between his Combine and NFL speed-through-the-cut curves on the same route families, each read against its own league; tested with the drill cut itself (Break G) against full-season separation over expected beyond a no-tracking baseline (log pick, official 40, weight, NGS score, TE), held out by draft class.
metric_name: Cut Match (per-receiver drill-to-NFL translation of the cut, yd/s gap net of rep counts, z) alongside Break G (push into the ground over the 1 s around the first real cut, g; ranks like speed shed into the plant, rho 0.70 per rep)
headline_number: Break G -1.2 in of career SOE per sd [90%: -3.8, +1.0], n=116; Cut Match +0.2 [-3.0, +1.9], n=106; IPW for having routes -1.0 [-3.1, +1.0]; 5 Combine-side metrics, smallest p 0.29 vs Bonferroni 0.01. What does translate: official 40 -> NFL top speed rho 0.48 [0.35, 0.60] and drill -> NFL speed through the cut 0.24 [0.07, 0.40]; Break G 0.04 negative, no better than the official shuttle (0.10, n=40).
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of the round-20 winner reframed on the translation angle and applying the judges' top_changes: (1) new per-receiver translation metric Cut Match, tested held out next to Break G; (2) hero Fig 1 now overlays each receiver's drill and NFL cut curves (6 receivers at evenly spaced Cut Match ranks), so the gap is visible; (3) one-clause title, one-line coach definitions under the bold finding, Break G tied to a laser/GPS-timeable proxy (speed shed into the plant); (4) named table of 3 receivers with drill rep vs NFL rep (in/slowest/out speeds, Break G both settings, gap, SOE); (5) Section 1 and 2 tables cut to 4 rows each, robustness rows to appendix.md; power sentence fixed ('68% at +/-3 in; 80% only for 3.5 in'), -3.8 primary vs -3.6 reliability-redrawn stated explicitly; (6) no-tracking benchmark for transfer (official 3-cone, shuttle), inverse-probability weights for having NFL routes (116 of 149), multiplicity count with Bonferroni; (7) day-3 compressed to two sentences with receiver-cluster bootstrap, LOCO, MDE (37 points) and a stated bar (lower bound above zero) that the list fails, so the queue and its man/zone, slot/wide splits and what-flips column moved to the appendix as a coin-flip tool; (8) verify.py now uses its own seeds and a second leave-one-class-out implementation (statsmodels WLS), rebuilds Cut Match, IPW and benchmarks from raw frames: 92 of 92 numbers reproduced (45 bootstrap quantities within Monte Carlo tolerance); (9) figure-text consistency, n and interval definition in every caption, dark neutral reference lines; 1,348 words, 4 figures + 3 tables.
open_risks: Still a null-result paper; the only positive translation (speed through the cut, rho 0.24) does not add separation beyond the baseline.
Cut Match rests on a median 14 sampled NFL breaks and 7 drill reps; odd/even reliability of the gap is 0.46, and the score is netted for rep counts, which a coach cannot reproduce by eye.
The day-3 list was removed from the body to satisfy the data-science judge; the football judge asked for it in the body with splits, so Football may score the usable-action dimension lower.
No-tracking benchmarks are thin (shuttle n=40, 3-cone n=32) because few receivers run them at the Combine.
Not blind: all three classes were seen while building the rounds; the drill-protocol prescription (re-stem hitch family at NFL speed) remains untestable with today's reps (4 of 265 matched).
